sections.heading: C — Penalties, suspension, alcohol
sections.markdown:
## C — Penalties, suspension, alcohol

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
Suspension parks your privilege awhile: pay up and prove legal presence to reclaim it after, but year-plus-expired licenses during suspension must also repass the two-part knowledge, road, and vision exams [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
Revocation kills the privilege outright: restoration means re-applying after the term with legal-presence proof, fresh vision, two-part knowledge, and road tests, plus fees [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
Courts or DMV must suspend or revoke for DUI, DUI injury, driving on DUI suspension, skipping a required interlock, lying to DMV, injury hit-and-run, vehicular manslaughter, DUI manslaughter, vehicle drug crimes, vehicle felonies, exam impersonation, or eluding police [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
Courts may suspend or revoke for reckless or aggressive driving convictions [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A02
The may-suspend list runs on: unlicensed operation, driving through non-DUI suspension or revocation, and refusing blood or breath tests when DUI-charged [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A02
DMV logs every court conviction for Virginians, hangs three, four, or six demerits on traffic offenses, and watches twelve-month and twenty-four-month point windows [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A02
Under-eighteen first demerit or belt convictions order a clinic, missed ninety-day completion suspends until done plus a fee, a second conviction suspends ninety days, and a third revokes a year or until eighteen, whichever lasts [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A02
At eighteen or nineteen, any demerit or belt conviction from those years orders a clinic [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: FXsec13F09
For drivers eighteen or older, twelve demerit points in twelve months or eighteen in twenty-four months requires a driver-improvement clinic completed within ninety days; missing that deadline causes suspension. Eighteen points in twelve months or twenty-four in twenty-four months instead brings a ninety-day suspension and a required clinic [FXsec13F09].
Source: [FXsec13F09 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A02
Medical review chases reported physical or mental fitness doubts across consciousness, perception, judgment, and motor skills, can demand doctor or vision reports and retests, and ends in suspension, restriction, periodic reports, or clean closure, with medical suspensions skipping legal-presence proofs [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A02
Registering forces an insurance oath or a $500 uninsured-vehicle fee [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A03
Two insurance failures draw suspension: skipping requested proof filings, and breaking coverage without surrendering plates [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A03
Child-support enforcement steers DMV to suspend for ninety-day or $5,000 arrears, or for dodging paternity and support process [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A03
Driving Virginia roads consents to breath tests on demand after probable-cause stops with drink or drug suspicion, and post-crash DUI arrests can land within three hours sans warrant anywhere [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A03
Refusing the breath test or blowing .08 or more triggers automatic suspension of seven days first, sixty days or trial for the second, and hold-till-trial for the third, with conviction penalties stacking and multi-DUI terms running consecutively [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A03
Open alcohol riding in the passenger zone, seats plus reach including unlocked gloveboxes, partly drunk with drinking signs showing, earns a drinking-while-operating charge [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A03
DUI with a seventeen-or-under rider aboard stacks a mandatory five extra jail days, a $500 to $1,000 extra fine, and on repeats eighty extra community-service hours, atop every base penalty [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A03
Driving through alcohol suspension seizes the car thirty days on the spot plus ninety more on conviction, while repeat unlicensed operation holds the car until licensed or three days, whichever ends first [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A03
Local law can bill DUI crashers up to $1,000 for the responders their wreck summons [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A03
Under-twenty-one drink-driving from .02 to .08 BAC costs a one-year suspension from conviction plus a $500 minimum mandatory fine or fifty-plus service hours [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]
